evidence.label: Equivariant Jiang–Su Stability for Amenable Actions in the Unital Stably Finite Case
Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability without elementary subquotients
Tracial projection methods and uniform property Gamma

headline: Claims amenable actions on Jiang–Su-stable algebras absorb the Jiang–Su algebra, plus three regularity theorems.
scope: Simple and nonsimple separable nuclear C*-algebras: Jiang–Su absorption, strict comparison, nuclear dimension, uniform property Γ, and amenable group actions.
plain: The Jiang–Su algebra is a small, infinite-dimensional operator algebra that behaves like a neutral element under tensoring. Algebras that absorb it are the well-behaved ones in the classification of nuclear C*-algebras. Four companion papers claim several regularity results, including the strict-comparison half of the Toms–Winter conjecture. The headline paper claims every amenable group action on a unital, stably finite, Jiang–Su-stable algebra also absorbs it. Lean checks the unital strict-comparison result and a uniform property Γ theorem.
doesNot: This does not cover nonunital algebras in the equivariant theorem, and Lean does not check the equivariant result or the nuclear-dimension theorem.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Xinhui Jiang and Hongbing Su, construction of the Jiang–Su algebra
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims to settle Szabó's Conjecture A in the unital stably finite case and parts of the Toms–Winter regularity problem.

explanation:
Start with 2-by-2 matrices. Put a 2-by-2 matrix inside a 4-by-4 one as a block repeated twice. Repeat to reach 8-by-8, 16-by-16, and so on. The limit of this chain is an infinite-dimensional algebra. Tensoring it with one more 2-by-2 factor just shifts the chain by one step, giving the same algebra back. That is absorption: A ⊗ D looks exactly like A.

The Jiang–Su algebra, written Z, is the gentlest algebra with this property. Jiang and Su built it as a simple, infinite-dimensional, unital algebra with the same invariant as the complex numbers[5]. It has no projections other than 0 and 1. A C*-algebra is Z-stable if A ⊗ Z is isomorphic to A. Finite matrices fail this: a matrix algebra has nuclear dimension zero but does not absorb Z[8]. Nuclear dimension measures how many simple pieces finite approximations need.

Z-stability links to comparison. In 3-by-3 matrices, a projection of rank one has normalized trace 1/3 and one of rank two has 2/3. Smaller trace means the first fits under the second. Strict comparison asks that trace sizes decide this order in general. Rørdam showed that Z-absorption forces a weak form of comparison[6]. The Toms–Winter conjecture asks for the reverse. The obstacle is to build Z inside an algebra knowing only how its pieces compare.

The second paper claims strict comparison implies Z-absorption for separable simple nuclear algebras that are not just compact operators[7]. This includes algebras with no unit. The fourth paper treats the unital case separately and completes the unital Toms–Winter equivalence[11]. It also answers Problem XXI of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White[10]. The third paper claims to prove Robert and Tikuisis's Conjecture C1: finite nuclear dimension implies absorption, with no elementary pieces[9].

The headline paper adds a group action. Szabó conjectured that amenable actions on Z-stable algebras should also absorb Z[1]. Amenable groups are those with nearly invariant finite sets, like the integers. The paper claims the unital, stably finite case[2]. It assumes no outerness, Rokhlin or UCT condition[3]. Nonunital algebras lie beyond its scope[4].

How sure is this? A computer proof checker called Lean has formal proofs for parts of the fourth paper. It covers uniform property Γ from tracial real rank zero, and Z-absorption from strict comparison for unital algebras. It also covers one stably projectionless case. The equivariant theorem, the nonunital comparison theorem and the nuclear-dimension theorem are outside Lean. No specialist review of the papers has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if it holds. Lean checks the unital strict-comparison and uniform Γ results, but not the equivariant headline theorem; no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: An algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, closed under adjoints and norm limits.
A simple, infinite-dimensional algebra with no projections except 0 and 1 that acts like a neutral element under tensoring.
An algebra A with A ⊗ Z isomorphic to A; it absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra.
Well approximated by finite matrix algebras, in a precise sense.
How many simple pieces the finite matrix approximations of a nuclear algebra need.
When trace sizes decide which positive element fits under another.
A group with finite sets that are almost unchanged by translation, like intervals of integers.
A way to split the identity into central pieces that cut every trace evenly.
